messages:
ingrid.prod: pagerduty -> KV cache eviction & continuous-batching spike alert for us-east-1. Observability shows cont-batch queue length and per-token latency jumping ~3-4x starting ~08:10UTC. Customers on Dedicated showing 5xx and high tail latencies. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Alert triggered: kv_cache_eviction_rate > 0.9 for 5m across layers. incident_id=kv-2001
deploy-bot: Canary failure detected for batch-config v2.3.7 -> auto-rollback attempted (partial)
nate.prod: I'm on it. pulling up model-impact dashboard. Initial filter: Llama-2-7B-instruct and Mistral-7B mostly, Qwen-7B shows spike for GQA workloads (prefix-heavy). MQA traffic less affected except when prefix prefetch enabled.
samir: attaching quick metrics snapshot:
```
metric: cont_batch_queue_len{model="llama-2-7b",region="us-east-1"} = 320 -> 1200
metric: token_latency_p95{model="mistral-7b"} = 95ms -> 420ms
metric: kv_eviction_rate=0.93
errors: 504_count=182 (10m)
```
maya-ml: this smells like the new prefetch heuristic + continuous batching interaction. Prefetch can cause heavy KV churn for prefix-heavy GQA requests on Qwen. Suggest disabling prefetch for Qwen and reduce cont-batch window from 80ms -> 30ms as hotfix.
leah-sre: agree. plan: 1) reduce cont-batch window globally to limit batch accumulation 2) disable prefix prefetch for Qwen model variant 3) enable failover policy to replay on smaller batching tier for affected customers. We should do a canary for 5% traffic then 100% if stable.
ingrid.prod: do we have a config update command?
deploy-bot: Use the control-plane api to patch runtime config:
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"patch": [{"op":"replace","path":"/cont_batch/window_ms","value":30}]}'
```
nate.prod: applying cont-batch window -> 30ms canary (5% traffic) now. patch id=patch-kw-2001.
leah-sre: monitoring dashboards. setting alert thresholds tighter.
(oncall-bot): patch-kw-2001 rolled to canary: success. 5% traffic.
samir: early canary metrics: cont_batch_queue_len down ~60% for canary hosts, p95 latency down ~40%. No immediate errors.
manual note: customer-ops -> major customer "OptimaFin" reported 504s, ticket#CF-12188. Notifying CS.
customer-ops: OptimaFin impact window 08:09-08:28UTC, intermittent 504s and timeouts for embeddings+chat. They're on Dedicated with Qwen variant and high prefix reuse.
maya-ml: while we let canary run, I'll prepare a model-specific tweak: for Qwen GQA flows disable prefix prefetch and pin KV cache TTL to 30s to avoid eviction storms.
leah-sre: ready for larger rollout if canary stable for another 5m. recommend increase canary to 25% then 100%.
ingrid.prod: can we also add a quick throttling rule per-customer to protect OptimaFin while we stabilize? Low friction: apply rate-limit to their key.
deploy-bot: Rate-limiter rule created: key=optima-* -> qps cap 30. Applied to gateways in us-east-1.
(5m later)
leah-sre: canary -> 25% rolled, metrics holding. cont-batch queue below baseline. Eviction rate dropping to 0.2.
samir: starting to see reduction in 504s; OptimaFin reports fewer errors, CS updated.
maya-ml: rolling Qwen model flags: prefetch=false, kv_ttl=30s. Rolling via model-flags service: command:
```
rz model-flags set --model qwen-7b --flag prefix_prefetch=false --flag kv_ttl_seconds=30 --rollout 50%
```
deploy-bot: model-flags rollout 50% success, tracking.
leah-sre: good. now proceed to 100% rollout for both config and model flags, keep throttles for sensitive customers for 1h.
ingrid.prod: moving to full rollout. patch-kw-2001 -> 100% at 08:35UTC. model-flags -> 100% at 08:37UTC.
(incident-bot): Incident update: mitigation applied; customer impact reduced. continuing to monitor for regressions. Severity degraded from S2 -> S3.
leah-sre: post-mitigation checks: p95 latencies back near baseline for Llama/Mistral, Qwen p95 improved ~60% on GQA flows. Some residual elevated KV misses but within acceptable window.
nate.prod: root cause hypothesis: interaction between new prefetch heuristic and continuous-batching window allowed prefix-heavy tiny requests to create high KV churn; cache TTL/eviction interplay caused hot shards to thrash under MQA-style access patterns. Hotfix combined both rate and config mitigations.
samir: logs snippet showing eviction storm pattern:
```
[08:12:09] host-12 kv_evict key_prefix=usr:optima:prefetch size=3456
[08:12:09] host-12 kv_insert key_prefix=usr:optima:prefetch size=4096
[08:12:10] host-12 kv_evict key_prefix=usr:optima:prefetch size=3200
... repeat 1000x
```
leah-sre: next steps: - run replay job to reproduce in staging with prefetched prefixes load - add circuit-breaker when eviction_rate > 0.7 to auto-reduce prefetch - add per-model prefetch flag default off for GQA-like workloads - write runbook entry for prefetched-prefix+cont-batch interactions
nate.prod: handing off to night oncall (nate.prod -> ingrid.prod -> leah-sre summary). Night oncall: leah-sre 08:50UTC takeover.
leah-sre: I have the summary and mitigation steps. I'll keep throttles for OptimaFin for one hour and then review. Leaving notes for postmortem.
ingrid.prod: thanks team. initial RCA draft: 1) regression introduced by prefetch heuristic 2) unexpected coupling with cont-batch window 3) TTLs/eviction thresholds too aggressive for prefix-heavy workloads 4) mitigation: cont-batch reduction + disable prefetch + per-customer throttles. Will schedule postmortem and link tickets. :white_check_mark:
